name: Franceville (1889–1890)
description: A vertical bicolour of white at the hoist and red at the fly, with a blue rectangle at the centre bearing five white stars in the shape of the Southern Cross.
history: The settlers of Port Vila declared the independent commune of Franceville on 9 August 1889 to escape the lawlessness of the Anglo-French naval commission in the New Hebrides, electing a president and adopting a red, white and blue flag with five stars. The commune was suppressed in June 1890.
